thread:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 4532 triggered -> service: inference-queue-service. Urgency: high. Acknowledgment required from inference oncall. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: PAGE FIRED: `inference-queue-latency` - sustained queue depth abnormal for 3m. Pager: @inference-oncall. Link: http://pagerduty.example/incident/4532

raj: Acked via PagerDuty, I'm on it. Jumping into metrics and logs now — will post updates. ETA 5m.

emma: seeing p95 generation latency spike from ~700ms to ~3.2s starting ~00:02 UTC. Error rate still low. Queue depth on kafka-topic `inference-requests` ~420 (normal ~20-50).

miguel: confirmed. Worker consumer lag growing. Canary worker pods show high CPU and lots of OOMKill restarts in the last 6m. Might be a recent model rollout? Checking deploys.

nora: no prod deploys in last 30m from CI. Could be a slow-down in GPU-backed inference nodes or a stuck batcher.

raj: running quick checks:
```
# consumer lag check
kubectl -n prod exec deploy/inference-consumer -- sh -c "python tools/check_lag.py --topic inference-requests"
# pod status
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference -o wide
```
Outputs: consumer lag 412 msgs, pods: inference-worker-5 (Running, RESTARTS 3), inference-worker-6 (Running, RESTARTS 7), inference-worker-7 (CrashLoopBackOff).

emma: logs from worker-7 show repeated traceback out-of-memory in tokenizer step. Example:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/worker.py", line 234, in process
    tokens = tokenizer.encode(request.input)
  MemoryError
```

miguel: that aligns with higher batch sizes being selected by the serving runtime. Some requests have long context. We've had a batching policy tweak landed yesterday to increase max batch to 256 for throughput. If a noisy request gets in, it can blow memory.

raj: action plan: 1) reduce batch max to 64, 2) restart crashed pods, 3) route a portion of traffic to fallback smaller-model to relieve pressure, 4) monitor consumer lag. I'll apply 1 and 2 now.

raj: applying config rollback for batching policy:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/serving-runtime BATCH_MAX=64
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/inference-worker
```

incident-bot: Action noted: config change and pod restarts initiated by raj.

miguel: pods restarting. inference-worker-7 back to Running. Memory usage back down on new pods.

emma: queue depth dropping slowly from 420 -> 230 in last 2m. p95 still ~1.6s but trending down.

nora: recommend routing 30% traffic to `small-model-v1` for 10m to speed drain and avoid client timeouts. I'll stand by to flip routing if needed.

raj: routing 30% now via canary rule. Command:
```
redwood route update inference-api --traffic small-model-v1=30
```

raj: initial effect: p95 global now 980ms, queue depth 120. Good. Customer errors? Support, any alerts from customer-facing SLO watchers?

emma: no elevated 5xxs on public endpoints. A few internal retries from SDKs observed but within retry budget.

miguel: note: we should also add an immediate guard to reject requests with context >32k tokens to avoid re-triggering memory spikes. Will prepare a quick filter.

raj: quick handoff — I'm going to babysit the routing and capacity for the next 15m, but I need to hand deeper investigation (heap dumps, reproducer) to emma. Emma, taking this over for post-incident root cause?

emma: taking it. I'll collect heap dumps from the affected pods and correlate with deployment changes. Leaving notes: batching policy increased yesterday (PR #8421), tokenizer memory usage high on long-context inputs, fallback routed. Continuing in thread.

nora: I'll draft a short status update for infra-status and customer-status page:
- Impact: delayed inference (elevated latency) for subset of requests, no customer-facing errors detected.
- Mitigation: reduced batch max, restarted worker pods, 30% traffic routed to smaller model.
- Next steps: flipping to full routing if lag doesn't drop below 50 within 15m; root cause analysis in progress.

raj: confirm: consumer lag now 48, p95 820ms. I will keep watch for 10m, then we can de-escalate to SEV-2 monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident 4532 acknowledged by raj. Current status: mitigation in place.

miguel: pushed quick request filter to block >32k token requests (feature-flagged). Will monitor for invocations.

emma: collecting heap dumps and saving to S3 at s3://redwood-logs/incident-4532/ for postmortem. Snapshot links: http://s3.example/incident-4532/heap-1.dump

nora: status update posted to infra-status and to #product-support with note to monitor customer reports.

raj: handing active monitoring to emma. I'm marking this as handed off: leaving notes -> queue largely drained, routing to fallback 30%, batch max 64, filter in place. I'll be available if escalation needed.

emma: I've got it. Continuing RCA. Will open postmortem ticket and include timeline, config diff, and suggested mitigation (revert batch change and add token-length guard).

nora: thanks everyone. Closing pager for oncall after handoff.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 4532 acknowledged by raj. Incident transitioned to 'mitigated' state pending postmortem.

raj: final ping — queue stable ~15, p95 ~750ms. Moving to monitoring only. If anyone sees customer impact, ping here or page inference-oncall. Good job team. :thumbsup:
